comments.author: @MuhammadAamirRazzaq
comments.text:
Having lived in Pakistan for over 40 years, this documentary mixes genuine local facts with outdated stereotypes and mislabeled media:
Train Roofs [08:26]: The claim that people in Pakistan "literally ride on top of train cars" is factually false. Roof-riding is not practiced here—that footage is clearly mislabeled media from holiday rushes in India or Bangladesh passed off as Pakistan.
Food Regulation [04:28]: Claiming street food operates with "zero health inspections" is completely untrue. Food safety is actively regulated by provincial bodies like the Punjab Food Authority (PFA) and KP Food Authority, which perform daily inspections, quality testing, and shop closures across all major cities.
Infrastructure & Sanitation: Contrary to the impression given, open-air defecation is practically non-existent in modern Pakistan, intercity highway and motorway infrastructure has expanded dramatically, and urban slum areas are gradually being addressed.
Economic Reality [01:32]: The video blames economic collapse purely on domestic mismanagement. While internal corruption, inequality, and non-civilian political overreach are severe issues, you completely ignored crucial external factors: decades of foreign geopolitical meddling (particularly US political intervention), post-COVID global economic shocks, and energy inflation triggered by the Russia-Ukraine war.
Constructive criticism of Pakistan's governance is valid, but relying on fake/mislabeled visuals and half-truths turns what could have been a balanced documentary into sensational propaganda.
